projects.title: Harvard CS50 Finance
projects.description: Built a web application through which users can manage portfolios of stocks. Implemented IEX’s API, which helps users search, buy, and sell stocks in real time. Created and manipulated multiple SQLite databases to display the user's portfolio value

projects.title: Stock Prediction
projects.description: Created a basic prediction model using supervised learning and linear regression to predict the stock price. Built functionality to predict a specific stock at a specific time period given by the user's input.Improved the prediction accuracy by using various hypotheses, resulting in up to 80% accuracy in the predicted value

projects.title: UC Berkeley CS61B 2048 Project
projects.description: Built the core logic of the game “2048", a computer single-player game developed by Gabriele Cirulli. Built functionality to determine game status, count the number of points, and update the highest score throughout the period to make the game more fun and interactive. Created and applied helper functions to manage and reduce the complexity of the project

activity.title: Your AI agents are only as smart as the data they can access—but copying that data across clouds is slow, expensive, and a governance nightmare. At Next Tokyo, we’re changing that. We’ve introduced major enhancements to our borderless Lakehouse. Built on open Apache Iceberg, we’ve added catalog federation (in preview) for AWS Glue, Databricks Unity, and Snowflake Horizon. Your agents can now query and act on multi-cloud data in-place without moving physical files or building fragile ETL pipelines. Check out the full blog post to see how we're reshaping the economics of enterprise AI: https://lnkd.in/dGa44-fn #GoogleCloud #DataAnalytics #ApacheIceberg #MultiCloud

Different decade, same job for us network engineers: keep the network boring! Thank you to everyone at Google Fiber who made the last ten years what they were.

I Quitted this year YC Startup School... But I don't regret it. This time last year, I was attending the first ever YC startup school in the world. Being one of the pioneering participants bring me a very exciting and unique experience. But this year, I'm not going there. Instead, I spent a whole month in Vietnam, went back and forth between cities, met a bunch of new friends, and learned a lot of new things. During the time, I was lucky enough to attend the GRAB the Future Hackathon, which eventually granted me a Data Analyst intern at Grab. Later, I went to the Agentic AI Build Week from GenAI Fund, where I built and integrated Muster Task Delegator into internal operations at KT One. Closing the month was an amazing time at the 2nd SEA Quantathon in Vietnam, where KT One was able to secured a 3rd place along with investment opportunities. Thank you for making my summer extraordinaries, my G Duc-Kha Vu , Long Le , Marc Jermaine Pontiveros, and also with a lot of friends we talked along the way. P/s: First time on live broadcast, would prepare better next time!
